title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Fever and chills

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 68-year-old man who presented to the hospital with a high fever and associated chills. Laboratory work and diagnostic testing were initiated promptly. A blood culture was performed, which subsequently returned positive for bacteremia. Based on the clinical presentation and stable vital signs, the physician determined that the patient does not have sepsis. The patient remained stable throughout the stay and was managed conservatively. He responded well to the initiation of oral antibiotics. He was cleared for discharge once he remained afebrile for 48 hours and tolerated his oral intake.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Bacteremia

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin 875mg orally every 8 hours for 10 days.

Follow-up:
The patient should follow up with his primary care physician in one week for a review of his clinical status and to monitor the completion of his antibiotic course.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, MD, 05/15/2026
explanations: Bacteremia without sepsis is coded R78.81 (no HCC), which is not a sepsis code: no sepsis code applies.

distractors.why: The provider documents bacteremia without sepsis.
